title: Define attribution for interleaved cache-hit batch merges
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: when requests from different clients (or routes) are merged by the serving runtime into a single token generation batch, and that batch contains requests that partially hit the KV/prefix cache, our current metering pipeline sometimes double-counts or misattributes token charges. This ticket defines unambiguous attribution rules for interleaved cache-hit + miss batches and implements them in the accounting pipeline and quota enforcer.
background: We recently observed discrepancies in per-tenant token usage on dedicated clusters when the runtime merges low-latency requests with prefetched KV cache hits. Investigations (see linked dashboard) show two classes of error: 1) cached token segments being billed at full compute token cost when coalesced with non-cached tokens, and 2) quota throttles firing against the wrong tenant when cross-tenant coalescing occurs in shared pools. Existing docs (metering design doc v2) are underspecified for interleaving semantics.
problem_statement: Define a deterministic, low-overhead metering model for merged batches that: (a) does not overcharge cached tokens, (b) attributes compute/IO cost to the correct tenant/route, and (c) integrates with the quota enforcer without adding per-request synchronous coordination that would harm latency SLOs.
proposal: Adopt a two-tier attribution approach: 1) Per-segment accounting: annotate batch response segments with cache-hit metadata at the runtime boundary (segment owner, cache_type, tokens_consumed). 2) Aggregation rules in the metering pipeline: cached segments are charged at 'cache token' rate and excluded from GPU compute charge; compute tokens are attributed to the original request owner. For cross-tenant coalescing in shared pools, attribution uses immutable request owner IDs attached at batch formation time. The metering pipeline will apply an idempotent aggregation step keyed by (owner_id, model_variant, billing_bucket, hour) to avoid duplicates from retries.
tradeoffs: Pro: precise attribution, minimal billing variance, clearer quotas. Con: requires adding small per-segment metadata to RPCs and modest changes to the metering pipeline. Risk: additional metadata increases message size and requires validation across dedicated/private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits per-segment cache metadata for all merged batches in shared pools
Metering pipeline applies per-owner aggregation and produces same-day reconciliation reports with <0.2% discrepancy vs baseline
Quota enforcer uses aggregated tokens such that no tenant sees spurious throttles due to coalescing
tasks: Add segment metadata (owner_id, cache_status, token_count, prefix_hit) to batch RPC (runtime)
Extend metering pipeline to consume segment metadata and implement idempotent aggregation
Add unit and integration tests for aggregation logic
Update billing reconciliation job to validate new attribution rules
Run a canary on a small shared pool and compare metrics to baseline for 72h
testing_plan: Unit tests validate that cached segments are marked and priced correctly. Integration tests simulate mixed-hit/miss batches and assert per-owner totals. Canary will run in eu-west-1 shared pool with synthetic traffic and a golden accounting job to compare against legacy billing for drift and latency impact.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime and metering PRs behind feature flag. 2) Enable flag in staging and run billing reconciliation for 24h. 3) Canary in eu-west-1 for 72h with 5% of shared-pool traffic. 4) Gradual ramp to 100% over 48 hours if metrics stable. 5) Post-mortem and doc updates.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: message size growth causes slight increase in RPC latency. Mitigation: pack metadata compactly and run perf tests; fallback option to only emit owner_id + bitflags. Risk: private deployments lag in schema upgrade. Mitigation: runtime will support backward-compatible RPC schema and metering will treat missing metadata as 'unknown' and fall back to conservative charge with a reconciliation ticket.
notes: Conversations with Billing team suggested adding a temporary reconciliation buffer to absorb early drift; agreed to a 48h manual check during rollout. Legal asked that we produce audit logs mapping cache hits to billing buckets for customers that request proof of charges.
